questions.stem: This echocardiogram with color Doppler demonstrates the labeled left-to-right shunt between the aorta and pulmonary artery. If left uncorrected, chronic pulmonary overcirculation from this lesion classically progresses to which complication?

explanation.summary: A patent ductus arteriosus produces a left-to-right shunt; chronic increased pulmonary blood flow drives pulmonary vascular remodeling and pulmonary hypertension, eventually reversing the shunt (Eisenmenger syndrome) with cyanosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: A patent ductus arteriosus produces a left-to-right shunt; chronic increased pulmonary blood flow drives pulmonary vascular remodeling and pulmonary hypertension, eventually reversing the shunt (Eisenmenger syndrome) with cyanosis.

questions.stem: On the pretreatment chest radiograph, the red arrow points to an abnormality at the right lung base that resolves after therapy (post-treatment film). What is this finding?

explanation.summary: Blunting of the costophrenic angle with a homogeneous basal opacity and meniscus indicates a pleural effusion, which clears on the post-treatment film.

questions.stem: This indirect immunofluorescence image of ethanol-fixed neutrophils is used to detect an autoantibody associated with respiratory autoimmune disease such as granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Which autoantibody does this test identify?

explanation.summary: Immunofluorescent staining of neutrophils (cytoplasmic c-ANCA or perinuclear p-ANCA patterns) detects ANCA, which is associated with the ANCA-associated vasculitides that frequently involve the lungs.

questions.stem: In this patient with severe carotid stenosis, the noncontrast head CT abnormality indicated by the arrow most likely represents which acute process?

explanation.summary: Carotid stenosis is a source of artery-to-artery thromboembolism causing ischemic stroke; early noncontrast CT may show subtle hypodensity, loss of gray-white differentiation, or a hyperdense thrombosed vessel.

questions.stem: Beyond the labeled normal structures, this chest radiograph most notably demonstrates which abnormality?

questions.stem: These fingertips show bulbous enlargement of the distal phalanges with loss of the normal angle between the nail plate and nail fold. What physical finding is shown?

explanation.summary: Digital clubbing is bulbous soft-tissue expansion of the fingertips with loss of the normal Lovibond nail-fold angle (>180 degrees). It is associated with chronic hypoxic and fibrotic lung disease, cyanotic heart disease, and certain malignancies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Digital clubbing is bulbous soft-tissue expansion of the fingertips with loss of the normal Lovibond nail-fold angle (>180 degrees). It is associated with chronic hypoxic and fibrotic lung disease, cyanotic heart disease, and certain malignancies.

questions.stem: These serial aortograms show a discrete narrowing of the aortic arch just beyond the left subclavian origin (black arrow), a balloon inflated across it, and the widened lumen afterward (white arrow). What is the diagnosis being treated?

explanation.summary: The focal narrowing of the descending aorta at the isthmus treated by balloon angioplasty is a coarctation of the aorta, an obstructive congenital defect. It classically produces upper-extremity hypertension with diminished, delayed femoral pulses.
explanation.whyCorrect: The focal narrowing of the descending aorta at the isthmus treated by balloon angioplasty is a coarctation of the aorta, an obstructive congenital defect. It classically produces upper-extremity hypertension with diminished, delayed femoral pulses.
